title: a16z Podcast: The Changing Culture of Open Source

reader_summary.source_label: From the episode notes — transcript not yet available
reader_summary.headline: The culture of open source has changed across generations.
reader_summary.overview: The culture of open source has changed across generations. Which makes sense given that open source powers so much of the software world today... and by the way, that's not just tech companies but hospitals and banks; it touches everyone.

key_points.text: The culture of open source has changed across generations.
Open source culture has also moved away from cults of personality and top-down models to drive the vision for open source projects.
So what does that mean for the governance of open source, whether it's by institution or foundation, or a "healthy" or "popular" project?
